Clock starts on-site when contract opens

Entire Save Your Ass prep speech
No attempt to lock a slot today
BOLDED list at top of email
"Any other questions before I let you go?"
Hours and how to reach us
top_strength: This was a well-organized, efficient discovery call — 8.7 minutes, tightly sequenced, and Erik signposted where it was going: "I'd like to just kind of break down the pricing structure. Talk to you a little bit about what goes into the pricing for us, how our clock works and then finally the estimate that I've got put together here for you." His probing on access was the best thing on the call. Rather than accepting the default, he explained the methodology and got the customer to correct it: "We like to take the distance that we can park you know how far away from the elevator we can park and then add that to the distance from the elevator to your apartment on each floor" — which surfaced that it's "a little wonky to get to the freight elevator" and moved the number from 100 to 150 feet on both ends. He was also honest rather than promotional on day rates, telling a self-declared price shopper that Sunday is "only $1 per person per hour, cheaper than a Monday through Thursday day or rate."
coaching_note: Lucas opened with "I mean, shopping around for price" and Erik never gave him a single reason to pick Einstein over a cheaper quote. No No Worries Damage Coverage, no Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee, no "no hidden fees" pitch — so the only thing this customer can compare on is $204 an hour, which is exactly the fight Einstein does not want. Then the close was given away: when Lucas said he needed to confirm freight elevators, Erik responded "if you end up wanting to move forward with Einstein... you can get back to us with the time." That hands the decision to the customer instead of removing the risk. The fix is one sentence he already knows how to say — there is no deposit, so lock the Wednesday slot now and move it for free once the elevators are confirmed. He used that exact play on the Kahn call the same afternoon ("did you want to secure a spot and we can shift it afterwards?") and it produced a booking.
phone_presence_notes: Natural, easy conversational register — "Cool man," "Alright, perfect man. Sounds like it" — used Lucas's name repeatedly and acknowledged his flexibility concerns without rushing, though there were no real empathy or humor moments.
